content.thinking:
I'm planning the pixel art proportions for the monster truck, working out realistic tire diameter and body dimensions, then setting up a chassis root joint with wheel positions relative to it.

Now I'm designing the hinge and steering joints for the wheels and doors, orienting the wheel cylinders so their axis aligns along the axle direction. I'm also setting up a box helper function for building parts attached to specific bones, and planning the color palette and tread texture for the tires.

For the tire tread, I'm generating lug boxes positioned around the cylinder's circumference and merging them into one geometry, built in local space relative to the wheel joint's position so orientation stays correct.

Using 16-sided low-poly cylinder for the tyre, with 16 lugs spaced at 22.5° so one lands exactly at the bottom for ground contact; checking the outer radius math so lugs stay flush with the tyre surface without clipping.

For the hub I'm adding a grey metal rim disc plus six small cylinder lug nuts merged in, then painting the sidewall as a ring pattern based on radial distance from the wheel center -- black tyre, a red stripe ring at radius 0.6, and a white raised ring at 0.7, with the inner hub region masked off from the paint.

Now I'm defining the tread face with dark grey plus mud-speckle noise, applying the paint texel at a 0.04 cell size, and adding a silver rim cylinder slightly wider than the tyre with a yellow center cap and nut details.

Next I'm moving to the chassis/body, shaping a Bigfoot-style pickup truck with axle track and tyre width dimensions set up for the overall frame.

I'm sizing and positioning the body relative to the tyres, adjusting centre offsets and half-widths so the tyres sit just outside the frame while keeping clearance between the body floor and wheel tops.

Now I'm laying out the chassis structure—frame rails, cross members, and front/rear axles—working out their positions and dimensions so the axle boxes align through the tyre hub centers.

For suspension, I'm planning four-link bars and coilover shocks connecting axle to frame, angled slightly, though since the wheels won't actually suspend I can treat the linkage as mostly fixed. Now I'm shifting to the body, roughing out the cab, hood, and bed sections for the pickup shape, defining the hood's forward extent and height.

Working out dimensions for the hood with a blower scoop on top and the cab split into a lower body section and a narrower greenhouse above it.

I also need the open truck bed with floor, walls, and a roll cage, plus bumpers, grille, glowing headlights and an amber roof light bar, chrome exhaust stacks rising behind the cab, and a paint scheme with flames over the orange-red base.

Working out the flame math...

I'm applying the cell-noise paint function to the body panels—hood, cab, bed walls, doors, fenders—then checking texel density against the painted surface area, including tyres, to decide the texture sheet should be 2048px for adequate resolution.

For windows I'm using a small pixel texture with a blue gradient and diagonal glints applied to thin glass boxes set slightly proud of the frame. For the doors, I'm setting up hinge joints at the front edge of the cab with a vertical rotation axis, positioning each door panel with its own painted body, window, and handle relative to the chassis.

For the wheels, I'm defining steering joints at the chassis parented to each wheel centre with a vertical hinge axis, then adding wheel hinge joints along the horizontal axis, making sure left/right conventions stay consistent (left side = +X).

I'm setting up a spine joint at the chassis as the root, then writing a small helper function for creating box parts that takes size, color, position, bone, and extra options, defaulting to the chassis bone. I'm also checking the type imports needed for Joint and Fill from the skeleton and context modules.

Now I'm planning rotated parts with options for rotation angles or direction axes, plus a merging helper that groups geometry by color for efficiency. I'm defining constants like a texel size and color palette, then sketching out a wheel-building function that computes position offsets and creates steering and wheel joints with names like steerFL, steerFR, wheelFL for front and rear wheels.

Modeling tire geometry...

Writing wheel rim details...

I'm figuring out layering so each wheel component pokes out slightly beyond the one behind it, and dirtying up the lower tire with brown noise to simulate mud splashes. Now I'm adding axle tubes and suspension pieces positioned between the hubs at each axle location.

For the drivetrain, I'm placing a boxy differential housing at the chassis centerline, a driveshaft rod running fore-aft, and coil shocks angled out toward each wheel.

Working out the shock spring geometry now: stacking small rotated tori along the shock axis to form a coiled yellow spring, mounted between chrome shock rods near each wheel.

Now I'm adding the suspension four-link bars connecting axles to frame points, a steering tie rod across the front axle, and defining the main frame rails and cross members under the body.

For the engine, I'm skipping a visible block but adding a chrome supercharger blower on the hood with an intake scoop, pulleys, and eight chrome injector stacks. Then I'm laying out the body shell itself: a dark floor pan and the hood as a large box positioned above it.

Now I'm detailing the front end -- a beveled hood top with a cutout for the blower, a grille box with a pixelated black-and-chrome bar texture, and a chrome front bumper with a tubular push bar made from vertical rod sweeps.

Still writing more body parts...

I'll skip the raked windscreen detail and instead add a roof panel with a light bar on top, placing amber glow boxes along its front face, then work out chrome door handles and mirrors, plus how the door panel relates to the side window plane.

Working out the door panel geometry now, matching its hinge position and extent to the cab's lower front edge so it continues the body paint and flame design, and defining the door joint parameters...

Now checking running board placement along the sides to make sure it clears the front and rear tyre positions without overlapping them, positioning it just above the tyre height.

Then I'm laying out the truck bed: floor panel, side walls, and tailgate dimensions and positions, checking that the rear tyres sit alongside the bed rather than colliding with the body width.

Now I'm adding a chrome roll bar in the bed using rod geometry for verticals, top bar, and back-brace, plus thinking through bed contents — a liner texture, maybe a small crate or toolbox, and a checkered flag on a pole made from double-sided planes.

Working out positions for the flag pole and bumper box...

Now I'm placing tail lights as small red glow boxes at the rear corners, and figuring out exhaust stack placement behind the cab, nudging the x and z coordinates to avoid clashing with the roll bar posts.

I'm detailing the exhaust pipe tips with bent rods, flared chrome caps, clamp rings, and small glow cones for flame effects, then noting fenders aren't needed for a monster truck, and planning a number decal texture on the doors.

I'll orient the decal plane to face outward correctly regardless of side, size it to fit the door, and add other details like a roof antenna with a pixel ball, a dark sun visor box above the windscreen, and decide to skip interior seat details since windows stay opaque.

Mirrors, red tow hooks, hood scoop, and under-body gear are quick additions, and I'll place a simple pixel flame or skull emblem decal on the tailgate rear face instead of the hood. Now I'm defining the glass texture...

Still defining paint logic...

Writing tire paint logic...

I'll keep the chassis color flat and simple rather than procedural, importing the glow helper for highlights, and need to make sure only actually-used imports (THREE, createBuilder, noise, cellPaint) stay in to avoid TS unused-import errors.

Setting up imports and color ramps...

Still shaping body paint logic...

I should also exclude greenhouse windows above y 2.0 from this treatment, and add a dark lip color near the bottom edge before the flame colors kick in. Now I'm writing a tire paint factory function that uses radial distance and noise to shade mud and rubber tones...

Still writing tire shader logic...

Now I'm sketching the wheel construction: lug nuts and bolts positioned locally around the wheel center using small cylinder geometries arranged in a circular pattern on each side, merged with the rim mesh so the bone joint stays centered.

I'm also planning joint types for steering, then adding decorative details like bolt rows, rivets, and chrome ring stacks via merged geometry grouped by color, aiming for roughly 150 parts total. I'm defining a helper function to simplify creating rod-shaped connectors between chassis points.

Positioning the door, cab, and greenhouse boxes with matching widths, then adding the mirror assembly as a rod and chrome box off the cab side, plus hood details like the blower unit.

Still placing hood parts...

Deciding on decals now—adding a skull design to the tailgate plus number markings on the doors and glass. Sketching out the pixel grid for the skull shape row by row to get the proportions right at 11x11.

Still writing pixel texture code...

Still writing texture and geometry code...

Now I'm positioning the roll cage hoop with chrome posts and diagonal braces, adjusting the flag pole's x-position to avoid overlapping the structure.

I'm sketching out the exhaust stack placement, frame rail colors, and underbody details, then working through the shock absorber geometry — coaxial spring coils around a chrome rod, interpolated along the suspension travel line with slight tilt.

I'm realizing the shock mounting towers might poke through the hood or bed floor depending on height, so I need to adjust the top position so it stays hidden below the visible floor line in both the front and rear positions.

Driveshaft and diffs visible underneath, skipping fuel tank but adding a gearbox box under the cab. I'm finalizing the joint helper signatures, color/paint types, and headlight housing geometry positioned just in front of the fascia.

Working out grille placement between the headlights, bumper box depth, and push bar rod positions so nothing clips into the headlight housings up front.
